alternatives_considered: Potential RFP to other RCM vendors
battlecards.why_selected: Agreed to reduce effective fee from 3.39% to 3.15% of collections and apply pricing retroactively while avoiding $9M early-termination penalty.
battlecards.contract_terms: 3-year addendum (effective 9/1/22) at 3.15% of net collections with retroactive credit, automatic renewals remain through Jan-2025.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Benchmark showed rates 40–60 bps above market; client threatened migration to athenaCollector or full RFP six months before contract expiry.
battlecards.switching_costs: ≈$9M contractual penalty plus system migration, data conversion and provider retraining.

battlecards.why_selected: Provided lowest total landed cost in BAFO, could service both Mid-Atlantic and Heartland regions and agreed to Net-60 terms with dedicated implementation resources.
battlecards.contract_terms: Multi-year distribution agreement (draft dated 8/22/22) covering inventory management, QBRs, implementation timeline, Net-60 payment terms.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Consolidating all regional volume (~$1.5M) and multi-round RFP created competitive tension among four distributors.
supplier_weaknesses: Higher minimum order quantities than some peers
battlecards.switching_costs: Formulary alignment, staff training on new ordering portal for Heartland sites.
battlecards.notes: Heartland region transitioned from Medline to McKesson; Mid-Atlantic remained with McKesson.

battlecards.why_not_selected: Could not match McKesson’s enterprise pricing or extended payment terms; limited resources for formulary management.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Threat of losing entire Heartland book of business.
supplier_weaknesses: Pricing not competitive enough in BAFO

battlecards.why_not_selected: Pricing and service fees higher than McKesson’s BAFO; fewer local distribution centers covering Heartland.
Could not meet target pricing feedback issued 5/4/22; limited commitment on inventory management resources.
Per-scan pricing out of market; unresponsive to scheduling requests; insourcing showed 18-24% lower cost.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Demonstrated cost comparison vs. salaried techs and recruiter model.
battlecards.switching_costs: Need to recruit/hire full-time sonographers and implement Staffmark support.
battlecards.notes: Transition to in-house recruiting expected complete by EOY 2022.

battlecards.why_selected: Provides flexible recruiting support at 20% utilization while Advantia scales internal capability; second-lowest cost scenario.
battlecards.contract_terms: Recruiter-on-Demand hourly model; no long-term volume commitment.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Compared against fully in-house salary cost and IT Imaging per-scan rates.
supplier_strengths: No fixed FTE cost when not used
battlecards.switching_costs: Can disengage with limited notice; low contractual lock-in.
battlecards.notes: Expected 20% utilization in steady-state to fill candidate pipeline.

battlecards.why_selected: Offered acceptable 10% reduction while maintaining existing phlebotomist staffing and LIS interface; operational change to Quest deemed disruptive.
battlecards.contract_terms: New pricing schedule effective 10/15/22; term aligned to 3 years with annual price review cap at 3%.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Quest BAFO was 19% below baseline, providing credible switch threat.
battlecards.switching_costs: Retraining staff, specimen pickup logistics, reconfiguring billing workflows.

battlecards.why_not_selected: Although offering 19% savings, changeover complexity and clinic preference led to retention of LabCorp.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Low-price BAFO used to secure improved terms with incumbent.
supplier_weaknesses: No existing phlebotomist staff in clinics
battlecards.switching_costs: Transition of lab pickups, IT interface development, patient instruction updates.
